review:
Town of Salem is presented somewhat in the style of an animated board game, pitting fifteen people against each other in a clever roleplay battle of wit, perception, strategy, and deception.

[u][b]A quick recount of a fun session I played.[/b][/u]
In a recent game, I was the serial killer. That means I can kill at night and can not be killed. All I have to do is keep killing people, keep deceiving them, and not leave any clues for them to suspect me. I won this specific game, because there was a player named Snoop Dogg and every time I killed someone, I would leave a "death note" with a vague dog-related reference on the victim - even some as obtuse as "Bow down before the Lion". This made people increasingly suspicious that this other player was the serial killer, without focusing any suspicion on myself. Yet, I (feigning to be a good guy) kept raising questions about yet *another* player, so that the town never had enough votes in agreement about Snoop Dogg to have him put on trial. Keeping Snoop Dogg alive meant I could keep killing with impunity. Until there were so few townsfolk left that I was able to kill Snoop Dogg, get away with it, and win the game.

[u][b]So what is the gameplay?[/b][/u]
When you start each game, you can pick new name. Some people choose generic and some are clever. It's the internet, so plenty are offensive. When the game starts, all fifteen players will be told what their role is. Each role comes with certain abilities, traits, alignments, and limitations. The goal is to play your role, while supporting your faction. Each role has different faction alignments. Some are aligned with the mafia and the town. Some are aligned with the town and witches. Some, like the serial killer, are aligned only with the survivors.

The game is broken up into rounds. Your activities are performed at night. If you're the serial killer, you kill at night. If you're the investigator, you investigate one person's information each night. If you're the mafia, you communicate privately with the other mafia and the godfather at night, about who to kill and then you kill them. If you're the jailor, you put someone in jail overnight. If you're the escort, you distract someone overnight.

Then there are limitations. For example, the serial killer can not kill the mafia's godfather. So if you choose to kill someone overnight, but are not able to, there's a good chance you (as the serial killer) have just identified who the god father is.

When the night is over, you get a tally of the dead and how they died. You can read their will (each player can write a will, which for some is just a clever or insulting quip, but for others is an on-going ledger of information they've gathered while playing, so that upon their death, other players are informed as to what that player knew).

Still in the day phase, everyone votes on who to execute, if anyone. If enough votes are tallied for an individual, that person has to plead their defense to the town (in their own words). The town can then determine if they find him guilty or innocent. If he's guilty, he is hung. After his death (as with all deaths), his name goes up on a visible list for all to see, along with their role. (As an aside, there are also mediums - who are the only players who can communicate with the dead players in chat, using their information for themselves or to share with the living to inform future judgments).

It will often play out something like this: Someone accuses a player of being the godfather. Everyone votes for that person. That person swears they are the sheriff and the town needs them. Nobody buys their lies. They hang him. Then the name and role appears on the grave sites... they were telling the truth! They [i]were[/i] the sheriff! Uh oh!

And then night comes again and we carry out the rounds like this, until almost everyone is dead and the town, mafia, serial killer, or other faction is left alive and declared the winner.

[u][b]There are a few small hurdles that may trip some up. They are worth dealing with.[/b][/u]
First, this is a free-to-play browser-based game that is now also on Steam for $5 USD. Those $5 are converted to ingame currency to buy cosmetic items like death animations or houses. There is no pay-to-win aspect to the game; only cosmetic items. You also accrue currency simply by playing, so you could play with no disadvantage whatsoever without ever paying a dime.

Second, the game requires you to install Adobe AIR, so if this isn't already on your system, it will direct you to install it before the game runs. You'll also need to create a game account. Click "register" from the game's interface to be taken to the web page where you do this. The page it takes you to is a sign-up for a forum account, which may seem confusing. Just do it, as the account is directly tied to your game login. When you're done, login to the game with those credentials.

Third, when you go to play a game, you'll have the options "invite friends" and "solo". This is very misleading, but if you click "solo", you will actually be entering the online multiplayer, which is what you obviously want.

[u][b]Overview.[/b][/u]
The game is addictive and allows for a lot of role playing and deception. Even with fourteen other total strangers. Depending on the mode you are playing, there are also somewhere between 15 and 30 different roles to be played. Vigilante, veteran, doctor, mafioso, framer, godfather, spy, jailor, sheriff, escort, serial killer, witch, werewolf, arsonist, executioner, survivor, amnesiac, forger, vampire hunter, vampire, janitor, disguiser, consort, consigliere, blackmailer, bodyguard, investigator, lookout, mayor, medium, retributionist, transporter, jester...

The game becomes a clever meeting of wits, suspicions, piecing together what you know about roles and how they interact with each other, lying, determining truth, banding together, and backstabbing. It is absolutely unique and so compelling that I played six hours straight the first time I launched the game.

The game is a no-brainer at the price of zero dollars, if you play the web version. Frankly, it's worth $5 USD for the Steam version, too. If you're unsure, try the web version and decide if you'd like to support the guys behind this game by kicking in the $5 on Steam and getting this version. It also doesn't seem like there are a lack of players. Even past midnight, there were more than 300 ongoing games being played by almost 4,000 players. I never waited to get into a lobby and lobbies are filled and launched into the game within about one minute.

I can't implore you enough to give this game a shot, if any of this sounds even remotely compelling to you.

I absolutely loved this game, with over 1000 hours dedicated to Ranked, but I just can't recommend it anymore.  It feels as though the devs have given up on the game, and after two years of waiting for them to change their course, so have I.

Some of the more specific complaints I have are:

1. An extensive data breach of millions of accounts back in January 2019.
2. Reports are player-managed and not incentivized, meaning most rulebreakers don't see their reports reviewed before they expire.
3. The rules constantly change, but these changes are listed on third party sites like Reddit, and are never mentioned in-game.  They also often include sections that contradict each other.
4. The last "season" (supposed to last 3 months) has been going on for over 18 months.  Seasons are a chance to rebalance the gameplay, reward players, and reset the scoreboards.  None of this has happened.
5. The ELO-based matchmaking system doesn't really work, and will occasionally pair players with vastly different (>1000) ELOs into the same game.
6. Coven Ranked is dead and has been for years.  The devs have done nothing to try and revive it.

These aren't problems you can solve overnight, but they also shouldn't take years to address.  Constant excuses of mobile development and engine rewrites preventing them from rebalancing roles, punishing rulebreakers, or resetting the high scores were rediculous, but what's far worse is that those problems still exist months after that development has concluded.

"We can't both be," I hissed.  The medium's vote wavered.

Playerbase, and the ban system.

I've introduced three friends recently, and each one of them got put off because they got reported for game throwing because they didn't know the way the role worked, e.g forgetting to write a will or performing their role.

Imagine you join as a jailor in your first game, you don't jail someone until night three because you don't notice the button, you don't write a will and you accidently execute a confirmed townie because a maffia convinced you to. Sounds like a pretty nice move from the maffia right?

The base game is alright.

[list]
[*]Classic mode is where most new players go. You have a very specific role list with very little variation, which allows you to start out by learning a few roles at once. The main downside of this mode is that it isn't all that replayable. The very limited role list doesn't allow much variation and doesn't give much claim space. Since this is the mode where most new people go, you can also easily find yourself annoyed at the incompetence of others once you start to learn the game.
[*]Ranked Practice is where most of the action takes place from what I understand. I remember back when I played ranked practice, it was possible for every role to appear. Sadly, they ended up making it impossible for most of the neutral roles to make an appearance. However, the Mafia and Town role lists are way more varied, giving Mafia more claim space and adding more replayability. People tend to also know more what they're doing, which is a nice plus.
[*]Town Traitor Mode seems to also be decently popular. Like in ranked practice, there is no variation in the neutral roles, but all Mafia and Town roles have a chance of appearing. In addition, 1 randomly selected townie now secretly works for the mafia, which is an interesting concept that switches up the game quite a bit
[*]All Any is where you'll probably find the most replayability in the long term. Every slot can be filled with any of the roles in the game. This does mean the role lists are often less balanced, but because you don't know which roles are in the game, you have a lot of claim space. It can be a chaotic mess, but darn if it ain't a fun one.
[/list]

However, the coven DLC is where the game really shines in my opinion

[List]
[*]Coven classic and coven ranked are both deserted, good luck finding players there
[*]Weekly gamemodes sees a good portion of players. Every week, one of 3 gamemodes can be played
[list]
[*]Lovers where 8 of the 15 people are split up into 4 lover pairs. If your lover dies, you die. If your lover wins, you win. The role list is pretty static, but contains a lot of neutral roles which is nice since not many modes tend to have a lot of neutral roles in them.
[*]In VIP mode, 1 town member is randomly selected to be the VIP. Every single townie will know who the VIP is. If the VIP dies, town loses and coven wins. It's a great introduction to the coven faction and always has 2 of the DLC neutral roles. The role list doesn't change much, but it's varying enough for a weekly gamemode.
[*]Town traitor is largely the same as the one from the base game. One random townie secretly sides with the coven faction. This gamemode has no neutral roles, it's purely Coven vs Town
[/list]
[*]Lastly, we have the gamemode where I spent most my time in, the main reason I still enjoy playing this game. Coven All Any. It's the same principle as normal All Any, but there are way more roles in rotation. The Coven expansion added a lot of roles and here you are able to see them all interact with each other. Basic all any, even though the role list varied every time, was still Mafia vs Town. Coven All Any however sees 3 major factions (coven, mafia and town) facing off against each other. And as if that wasn't enough, you also have this large variety of neutral roles all with their own objectives, thrown into the mix. Even though this gamemode tends to be chaotic, I'm rarely left feeling like there was nothing I could have done to save the game. Even tho the odds can easily be stacked against you, there is almost always still a way to win. It feels great, grabbing the victory for town when there were only 2 townies in the game. I've had games, where I was the only evil left and I managed to convince town that I was one of them, getting a lot of townies lynched in the process and sneaking the victory.
I can't stress enough how much I love playing this gamemode. The people generally know what they're doing, there are very little trolls and it feels fresh every match I play
[/list]

tl;dr:
base game is good, coven DLC is better. Hope to see you in Coven All Any

Before I get into the review, allow me to say one thing. THIS GAME IS COMPLICATED AND YOU WILL DIE A LOT BEFORE YOU FIGURE IT OUT. As someone with a decent amount of playtime and a grasp of how the playerbase and game works, allow me to give you some tidbits before you download this game. It will help you a LOT.

1- Always have a Last Will written, stating what your role is and what you do every night.
(EXAMPLE BELOW:)

[NAME] the [ROLE, FAKE ROLE IF YOU ARE EVIL]
N1 (stands for Night 1): [what your role did that night on which player]
(repeat the same process for nights 2, 3, and so on).

2- Some basic vocab. There are some basic vocab words you should know so you don't get confused.
-inno (means vote innocent in trials)
-vfr (vote for role)
-gf (short for godfather)
-BG (short for bodyguard)
-dusa (short for medusa)
-med (short for medium)
-will (means last will, if they ask you this you post your will to the chat)
-arso (short for arsonist)
-ww (short for werewolf)
-maf (short for mafioso/any mafia role)
-exe (short for executioner)
-vet (short for veteran)
-psy (short for psychic)
-retri (short for retributionist)
-necro (short for necromancer)
-CL (short for coven leader)
-hm (short for hex master)
-Pm/Pmer (short for potion master)
-TK (short for town killing)
-TS (short for town support)
-TP (short for town protect)
-TI (short for town investigative)
-MK (short for mafia killing, which is mafioso/godfather)
-TP chain (where two town protects go on each other to create a nearly invincible combo at night)

3- Do not just claim your role as an evil. If you're evil, lie in your last will and if the town asks for your role, don't say "oh im the mafia," that's a one way ticket to the rope.

4- Any town investigatives except Lookout need to post EVERY DAY (except day 1 because you have nothing to post then). If you're a sheriff and you wait until you find someone suspicious, then people are going to be suspicious of you instead. Finding people innocent or seeing nobody visit someone is still information, and can help to sus out fake visiting claims or some neutral roles!

5- Don't be annoying. For real, I don't know how many people try to be annoying or rude without being a Jester (whos goal is to get lynched), but it's a lot. If you're making the game bad for people without being a jester, then just shut it and let people play. Plus, you'll get reported if you go over the top with things, so i'd advise against that.

6- Survivors, unless confirmed, are always suspicious. Some people on Day 1 will say "Day 1 surv" or "Day 1 survivor claim." Have any investigative of your faction check them IMMEDIATELY. Most of the time they're neutrals/evils trying to fake claim survivor to not get lynched. Some are real, and some are even hidden mayors who are planning to surprise reveal later in the game. 90% of them are fake, but if they are confirmed by your faction's town investigative/s, reach out to them late game and ask for help.

I hope these little bits of info will help you in this game, and ensure that you don't act like me and claim survivor on a list without survivor because I was clueless... oh by the way, if you want to support the game more, buy the coven expansion DLC! It adds a few roles listed in the vocabulary (necromancer, coven leader, medusa, potion master, and the hex master, along with the poisoner whom I haven't mentioned yet) and many more neutrals such as Guardian Angel, Plaguebearer, Pirate, and even some new mafia/town roles. Coven All Any (CAA for short) is one of the most played formats in the game, and it's a whole lot of fun! We all could use some new players there or even in the official formats! I spent 30 minutes writing this review, so I hope it's worth your time reading it! Have fun playing one of the best murder mystery games on Steam to date!

BTW, to the one guy who said it's just a guide, I thought it would be more helpful to write in the review section, as a new player just downloading the game would more likely look at reviews than guides!

First off, as you can tell by the number of hours that I put in the game, Town of Salem is a game that I very much enjoyed playing, although it was mostly first 40 hours. Once past those 40 hours, the scroll update fell upon Town of salem.

I would have recommended the game without a doubt before the update that introduced the scrolls.

Town of Salem is a fun game(similar to the Werewolf game), that requires you to be deceitful and think logically in order to win. You have to think strategically your every move, choose who to trust carefully. You get a role at the start of each game, with its own objectives and skills.

Most roles are fun and require a unique way of playing it. The townies are the most numerous and have to work together, the mafia must also work together, but in secret and most of the neutrals have their own agenda.

The two main game types allow for some very fun games. 

The classic game type forces you to play with a given set of roles that make for a balanced game.
The custom game type let the host decide what the roles are going to be, which adds a lot of replayability and diversity to the game.

If you like the Werewolf type of game, I think you'd like town of Salem.

However, I cannot recommend Town of Salem as of right now.

Since the scrolls were introduced, the game is a lot more frustrating.

The scrolls are in-game items that allow you to boost your chances of getting a specific role.
For instance, I can boost my chances of getting the role "Serial killer" from 7%(the default value) to 52%. 

This will logically decrease the odds for all the other players, from 7% to 4% if only a single person has a scroll. Once you get the role you wanted, it will burn one scroll of that specific type.

How do you get scrolls? You have to buy them for the most part. They each cost 200gold, and although you can get gold by playing the game, it is far easier and faster to just pay for gold with real money.

I don't have that big of a problem with the cosmetic purchases, like the different skins, houses ,etc, even though they can somewhat affect the balance of the game, as, if you're playing with a friend, you can tell more easily who that friend could be by looking at the different skins.

But the scrolls really messed up Town of Salem.

Since the scroll update, I get a lot more often the boring roles simply because I have a very low percentage of getting them due to other people using those scrolls.

I already bought the game, it is not a free to play on steam, I already for paid, there is no reason why an in-game purchase should affect the balance of the game. I understand that for the browser version they would add it, as it is free-to-play, but there's no reason why it should be there for the steam version. It doesn't make the game pay to win, it makes it pay for fun. Remove the $5 Town Points and let the game be fair again. 

While it was more tolerable back before the update to get the boring roles simply because everybody would have to get them at one point, but the chances of getting them were fair, unlike now. You could still expect to get a fun role in the next game. Not anymore. It's rare that I find a game where all the odds are 7% for every single role.

Furthermore, leavers utterly destroy the game. When you start a game and half of the townies are gone, it breaks everything, as the town has no chance of winning right off the bat. There isn't any penalties for people who leave the game. Therefore, you can expect at least 2 people per game who will leave during the first round, and more afterwards.

To make it worse, a role(medium) is all about interacting with the dead townies to get some clues as to who is what, but since most people just leave straight away, it makes it pratically useless in most games. 

In conclusion, Town of Salem is a fun game, even considering the very annoying quitting, but I'll only recommend it once the damn scrolls are gone and the devs add some penalties for quitters.

In the present circumstances, it is only a matter of time until another "Werewolf" game comes out on steam, without anything similar to the scrolls, at which point, Town of Salem will likely become deserted.

This is one of those games that has no middle ground. Either it's exciting and victorious, or frustrating and stupid. When games go well (whether they're in your favor or not), it's a great multi-layered cat and mouse. But more often than not you'll be dealing with AFK towners or instant leavers.

Y'see, there's certain roles that are still useful after death. Mediums for example can pass intel between living players and dead ones. Unfortunately, once people die there's a 70% they just leave the game entirely (which also sacrifices any coins they'd earn by remaining - something that's used to not just buy cosmetics but also scrolls which allow you to boost up your chances to get certain roles).

This makes it fairly difficult to learn the game. I have 35 hours played and I've only learned in the last ten to have the Town of Salem wiki open on my second monitor and just type in whatever role I get and try to strategize quickly based on what I can read in safer moments. Because the community itself sure isn't going to help.

Joining the discord does help a bit, though you can't discuss ongoing games. (It might out who you are if discord chatters happen to be in the same game, thus breaking that round a bit). I've been continually stuck in situations wondering who people know what and in my dozens of hours, I can almost never tell when people are actually lying about anything. Every single game turns into a clusterfuck of "he said she said". I was once in a Coven All/Any where two vampire hunters were screaming at each other because one person apparently copied the other's will. Turns out they were both true VH's and we just ended up lynching them both.

There's a lot of frustrating moments like that, but as I opened this review with it can lead to some heroic moments. Like how I tricked a winning werewolf that I was a survivor (a role that wins with anyone at all), having doused them with gas that previous night as they rampaged against the opposition, winning me the game. Or any time you can successfully pull of winning as a jester, whom the only goal is to get lynched properly. At that point you get a victory regardless, a role that's specifically designed to mix things up and look as suspect as possible without being too obvious. Or being in a full mafia game and successfully spinning tales and lies as the town lynches themselves.  Or that one time I resurrected a simple lookout that came back with vital intel and essentially carried the entire game to a townie victory with like, nine of us still around.

It can be great fun, but the toxic community taints this. You'll find that "Stupid/lazy/idiot town" fairly common in chat. I'm a bit more sporting, and typically realize that it's not always the town being dumb, but more that clever bad guys are just weaving convincing lies. I wish more people saw that. Despite my hour count, I still consider myself "new" and there's plenty of roles I know next to nothing about, and so many situations arise where I am just silent and dumbfounded at how anyone knows anything at all (especially in all any - one of the game's more popular modes).

So it's a lot to think about. Be prepared for some confusion and toxicity... punctuated with great moments of hilarious triumph. Good with the bad.

So - here's the thing.  I've been playing Town of Salem since it was only a browser game.  I used to LOVE it, as you can probably tell from my 293 hours logged (and that's just from when it came onto Steam, I shudder to think how many of my highschool hours were spent on this game).

Now...well, not so much.  To be honest, other similar games (that, yes, are free...) have overshadowed Town of Salem.  One is definitely Werewolf Online, which is a mobile game with a very similar concept but instead of the mafia it's werewolves...and the roles are different but.  Only slightly.  The thing that makes WWO SO much more attractive is the quality of life stuff that you hardly notice - yet it really has made all the difference.

A big issue I have in ToS is the balancing.  They've absolutely ruined roles that used to be my favorite - namely Spy and Sheriff, but plenty of others.  Spy in particular bothers me - the whole point was that blackmailer and spy were equivalents.  What's the point if only the mafia can read whispers?  And on that note, it's frankly pretty much impossible for the mafia or the neutral killer role to win anyways.  The whole thing is a mess.

They've ripped certain roles to shreds...to the point that when I took a two week long break, and I came back, I was so baffled with some of the changes I couldn't always keep up with what was happening.  I shouldn't have to go track down a log of changes constantly - and honestly, every strategy I built up for roles over the years is obsolete at this point.  It gets...frustrating.

Meanwhile, in WWO, when changes are made to roles they detail it in a place other than some obscure forum post, and even when I stopped playing it for a month, I was able to pick it up again easily despite several new roles being added.  Additionally. the DLC in ToS just made everything super convoluted.  I like the concepts of the roles but c'mon - making people pay for it when new roles are added constantly in a free mobile game with no trouble?

The biggest downfall of Town of Salem for me is that it has not updated for 2020.  Everything *feels* like an old game when I play (and it's not like they've actually added any content other than what, skins??), and that's fine, but not when new competitors are out there and more fun.  The community *feels* like I'm back in middle school when I play.  That's not a good thing.

If you're looking for a game like this, try WWO.  It's not "Mafia," but it's a whole lot more fun than this game anymore.

Town of Salem is a Strategic Elimination game that's set the the town of, well, Salem, back when the witch trials were very much alive.

This was a browser game in the past for quite some time, but December 15th is when it's mark on Steam came along. I played the browser version pretty extensively, and it's a very fun game to play because the outcome solely depends on player interaction and decisions.

See, you have these various roles, all with different alliances. Townies try and work together to survive and find out who the bad guys are. The mafia are their own group, trying to eliminate anyone who isn't them. And then the neutrals are people trying to achieve their own goal, neither with townies nor mafia. 15+ roles exist in the game, and they can all have a huge outcome on any game.

What's the catch? You have no idea who is what, so you need to use your smarts and think about whether to trust the people you're with or not. Each day, there's a discussion, then there's voting. If one person is voted to be lynched, they have a chance to defend themselves, then the town decides whether that person is guilty or innocent. The game then transitions to night, where the action happens. People can be stabbed, moved, killed, distracted, just about anything can happen at night, as careful as you may be. The game ends when either the Townies or Mafia wins (Neutrals are rare cases.)

This is why I like this game so much. Like I said, it depends heavily on human interaction, which is what keeps every game fresh and alive. You're always given a random role at the start of a new game. You can pick classic mode where there's a set list of roles, and all 15 players fufill one, or you can do "All Any" where you don't know what roles exist, and that makes it an even bigger mystery.

Overall, Town of Salem is an awesome game to play just for the suspensefulness and the fresh variety with every game, I really recommend this game.
